output.brief:
The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by the vendor's 3 March edge rule-pack update, not by release 6.14. A new rule (AUTO-LIB-17) blocks password-login requests that carry the nettle-http user-agent and have no edge session cookie. The Android app uses that library for all its API calls, so the rule blocks the app's own password logins with HTTP 403. Evidence: the extra failures began at 10:41 UTC on 3 March, one minute after the rule activated. They appear on every app version, including the 95% of users still on older versions, and on every Android OS version, whether or not the March patch is installed. Quick-unlock is unaffected, and iOS and web are unaffected. About 41,300 blocked installs had mostly logged in successfully before, so these are real customers, not bots. Only 5% of attempts were on 6.14 at first. Rolling back 6.14 would not help.
Next steps: ask Corvane to switch that rule to log-only on the password path, keeping rate limits, lockout and other rules on, then check that password success returns to about 96%. Don't raise bot sensitivity or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Tell the Head of Digital Channels that no rollback is needed. Contact-centre call volume is only loosely tied to this, since fee notices were also mailed that week.
